entry_state: The event/report separation now covers inventory quantity, asset age, working-capital contracts, currency, entity-level liquidity, taxes and reporting boundaries. A same-day financial change can invalidate a prior remedy finding even if its date still matches, and an annual close must preserve unpaid claims and relevant memory. The next passage examines conversion and control.
exit_state: Event histories connect claim extinction, share creation, control and dated liquidity; closing totals alone cannot establish an executable path. The compression chapter distinguishes storage sharing from economic equivalence and derives a finite-horizon sufficient condition preserving joint successor state, observations and outputs under common feasible information-based policies. A finite lending example shows why marginal equality is insufficient.

observations.finding: The conversion example removes the old claim before assigning 120 new shares and a three-quarter ownership fraction, under explicit supplied rights. The 10+20-25 cash example distinguishes a valid closing balance from infeasible payment order. The report procedure retains unresolved accounting consequences rather than balancing them away.
observations.disposition: retain; this completes the event chapter diagnosis without a new defect

observations.finding: Representation size, answer size, three graph meanings, immutable shared prefixes and existential projection are separated. Eliminating z from x=z+1 and 0<=z<=2 correctly retains 1<=x<=3, and threshold regions preserve the equality case.
observations.disposition: retain; no general polynomial-time or universal compression claim is made

observations.finding: The stochastic aggregation condition preserves the joint pushforward of successor state, observation and requested output, equal feasible actions and current outputs. Its induction explicitly requires consistent initial information and retained policy memory. The lending example produces +2,-4,0 with probabilities 9/20,1/20,1/2 and demonstrates failure of marginal-only comparison.
observations.disposition: retain local sufficient-condition argument; source theorem and implementation conformance remain separately bounded
